whatItFakes: The web's uninsured-share links (unemployment, Medicaid expansion, the work requirement, marriage equality) and the Medicaid medical-debt link move the web's own health.uninsured-pct number; no person's or counted household's coverage decision reads the factor.
why: The coverage record (modules/coverage.ts, counted households included) is on branch claude/coverage-counted (PR 5475) and not on main; the coverage code belongs to another session.
replacement: Once the coverage record is on main, the coverage decision reads webFactorFor("health.uninsured-pct", subject) with the moderators already in links.json (unemployment by sex and age), and medical debt reads the coverage record.
resolution: The coverage review (modules/coverage.ts, holdersToday) reads the web's factor for health.uninsured-pct for each worker's age and sex, full and counted alike, so the running uninsured-share links (unemployment, Medicaid expansion, the work requirement) change who holds an employer plan, by coverage record; proved by src/core2/coverage-web.test.ts. The medical-debt link and the marriage-equality link are registered on their own in SG-EW-HEALTH-medical-debt-reader.

whatItFakes: The Medicaid expansion to medical debt link (medicaid-expansion-to-medical-debt) moves only the web's own finance.medical-debt-in-collections number; no household's books hold a medical debt, so no one's money moves with it. The marriage-equality-to-coverage link has no running cause (the law has been national since 2015, link status cause-cannot-vary, the CTO's grade of Oct 29), so it moves nothing.
why: No household or counted group records medical bills or debts in collection, so there is nothing for a debt decision to multiply by the web's factor.
replacement: A medical-debt record on the household's books, decided from the household's own coverage record times the web's factor, which the medical-debt link then reads like the coverage links.

whatItFakes: Every death now carries a cause (overdose, youth firearm homicide, firearm suicide, motor vehicle, other) from NCHS 2023 shares by age, and the web's overdose, youth firearm and traffic links move those shares. What stays unwired: deaths under age 10 from firearms (the source reports none under 10, so the child access law reaches no toddler), the age split inside the 10 to 24 firearm band (ages 20 to 24 take the band's share although the web acts to 19), and counted people have no substance-use-disorder condition so none ranks first for an overdose.
why: The source tables give firearm deaths for ages 10 to 24 as one band and report nothing under 10; drug overdose deaths are reported from 15; counted people hold no conditions.
replacement: Single-age firearm and overdose death counts from CDC WONDER (underlying cause, one-year ages 0 to 24), and a condition record on counted people.

whatItFakes: Child asthma (gas-hookup-ban-to-child-asthma), Medicare out-of-pocket drug cost (drug-negotiation-to-out-of-pocket) and low birth weight from drinking-water violations (water-violations-to-infant-health) move only the web's number. (A teen's past-month cannabis use is now the health engine's record: SG-HEALTH-youth-cannabis-record-unread.)
why: No condition, prescription or birth-weight record exists for a child's asthma, an enrollee's drug spending or a newborn; condition-pack.ts holds adult chronic conditions only.
replacement: A childhood asthma condition and Part D spending on the household's books, each decided from the engine's own records times the web's factor.

whatItFakes: Congestion to premature births (congestion-to-premature-births), heat to deaths (heat-to-deaths) and eviction to hospital visits (eviction-to-hospital-visits) have no researched size, and coverage to blood pressure (coverage-to-blood-pressure) and a recession to total mortality (recession-to-total-mortality) find about zero, so nothing moves.
why: Three links are unsized in links.json and no producer exists for premature births, heat deaths or hospital visits; the two about-zero links run at size 0.
replacement: Sized links from fetched research, then the death and birth engines read them like the wired ones.

whatItFakes: Coverage to catastrophic bills (coverage-to-catastrophic-bills) and depression (coverage-to-depression); childhood food stamps to adult health (child-food-stamps-to-adult-health); the earned income credit to low birth weight (eitc-to-low-birthweight) are person-level links with no cause recorded on the person.
why: A person's coverage history, displacement, weekly hours, childhood benefit years and a birth weight are not stored.
replacement: Records on the person for each cause, read by the health engine's hazard like the web's death factor. The reader is the monthly look in src/core2/modules/health.ts (refreshWebFactors), which books a per-person factor from health-own.ts (plan.own): coverage-to-mortality-55-64, job-loss-to-death-risk and long-hours-to-heart-and-stroke are read that way now (carriedBy in data/research/outcome-web/links.json), and the links still waiting here are read the same way once the person's record exists (a stored coverage history for catastrophic bills and depression, childhood benefit years, a birth weight).
